title: Uncertainty limits for post-selected metrology
abstract: For unitary transformations, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of a pure state is given by the uncertainty of the generator in that state. In post-selected metrology, the QFI is given by a modified expression describing conditional quantum statistics of the generator. Here, we show that the conditional generator uncertainties defined by post-selected QFI correspond to Ozawa-Hall uncertainties known from the theoretical analysis of quantum measurements. The post-selected measurement outcome updates the generator uncertainty according to the quantum statistics of that outcome. Enhancements of QFI beyond the maximal uncertainties of the generator eigenvalues are possible because post-selection tends to concentrate the largest part of the initial generator uncertainty in low probability outcomes of the post-selection measurement. Anomalous conditional uncertainties thus explain the extreme sensitivities that can be achieved in post-selected metrology.
summary: This paper analyzes the uncertainty limits in quantum metrology when post-selection measurements are used. It proves that the achievable precision is governed by the Ozawa-Hall uncertainty associated with the measurement outcomes. The key finding is that post-selection can enhance sensitivity beyond standard limits by selectively amplifying certain quantum fluctuations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental uncertainty limits governing quantum estimation precision when post-selection measurements are performed on a quantum system.
main_result: It shows that the achievable precision (QFI) in post-selected metrology is determined by the conditional Ozawa-Hall uncertainties associated with the measurement outcomes.
method: The analysis involves deriving the post-selected QFI by relating it to the conditional quantum statistics of the generator, specifically utilizing the Ozawa-Hall uncertainty formalism.
model_or_system: The study models parameter estimation for a unitary transformation $\hat{U}(\phi) = \exp(-i  rac{\phi}{\hbar} \hat{A})$, where $\hat{A}$ is the generator. Simple examples use two-level systems, while advanced analysis employs ancillary qubit systems.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Ozawa-Hall uncertainty ($\epsilon^2_A(m)$), and anomalous imaginary weak values.
important_parameters: The unknown phase shift ($\phi$), the generator uncertainty ($\Delta A^2$), and the post-selection probability ($P(m)$ or $\eta$).
main_assumptions: The enhancement mechanism relies on the ability to concentrate quantum fluctuations into low-probability post-selection outcomes, and the analysis assumes the validity of the Ozawa-Hall uncertainty definition for conditional statistics.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the relationship between QFI and generator uncertainty for unitary transformations. It then introduces the post-selected QFI and links it mathematically to the Ozawa-Hall uncertainty. The core development involves demonstrating how post-selection leads to enhancements beyond standard limits, often illustrated using ancillary qubit systems and weak value calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework connecting measurement back-action (post-selection) to fundamental limits on precision, which is crucial for designing quantum sensors and understanding the limits of quantum metrology.
